<pasted_content id="eda4">
## User Story
As an event host or attendee, I want a reminder email 24 hours before a booked meeting so I arrive prepared.

## User Scenario
A meeting is booked for Thursday at 2:00 PM. On Wednesday at 2:00 PM, the host and attendee receive a reminder email with start times and location/video links

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Confirmed meetings booked at least 24 hours in advance automatically schedule a reminder to send exactly 24 hours before the start time.
2. The system successfully emails the host and attendees a message containing the event details, their local time, the meeting link,  and reschedule/cancel options.
3. If a meeting is canceled or rescheduled before the reminder triggers, the system automatically removes the pending reminder or updates it to reflect the new start time.
4. Automated tests must verify that reminders are correctly scheduled, updated, canceled, and delivered.

## Out of Scope
- Configurable reminder timings or per-event toggles (fixed at 24 hours for this issue).
- SMS or WhatsApp reminders.

## Open Questions
- Should we send only the 24-hour reminder, or include a 30-minute one?
- Should hosts receive these reminders by default, or only attendees, to prevent inbox noise for busy hosts?
</pasted_content id="eda4">

 PR DESCRIPTION: 

<pasted_content id="eda4">
Closes #66 

## Explanation of Changes
When an event is exactly 24 hours out, the host and the attendee will receive an email notifying them that their event is 24 hours out.

## New tests
`packages/emails/templates/booking-reminder-email.test.ts` 
`packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/scheduleBookingReminderEmail.test.ts`
`packages/features/tasker/tasks/sendBookingReminderEmail.test.ts`

These new tests check that the email is delivered exactly 24 hours out. Additionally, these tests check that if the event is rescheduled or cancelled, the email delivery is cancelled or adjusted accordingly.

## Design
When an event is cancelled or moved, how should we handle this?

### Decision 
When an event is deleted, the email notification should be cancelled. If an event time is changed, the initially set delivery time for the email should be changed to the new event time, assuming the time is more than 24 hours out.

### Alternatives considered
When an event is rescheduled to less than 24 hours out, the email reminder should be sent out immediately.

### Rational
We shouldn't send out a reminder if the event is edited to have a start time less than 24 hours because this behavior would only be seen here, meaning these email reminders *only* get sent out less than 24 hours before the start time under this specific circumstance, which we don't want.

### Consequence
If an event is edited to less than 24 hours out, the user and attendee don't get an email. 
</pasted_content id="eda4">

+import type { CalendarEvent, Person } from "@calcom/types/Calendar";
+import renderEmail from "../src/renderEmail";
+import AttendeeScheduledEmail from "./attendee-scheduled-email";
+
+export default class AttendeeBookingReminderEmail extends AttendeeScheduledEmail {
+  protected async getNodeMailerPayload(): Promise<Record<string, unknown>> {
+    const payload = await super.getNodeMailerPayload();
+    return {
+      ...payload,
+      // The invite was already delivered at booking time; re-attaching it would prompt a calendar update
+      icalEvent: undefined,
+      subject: this.t("booking_reminder_subject", {
+        title: this.calEvent.title,
+        date: this.getFormattedDate(),
+        interpolation: { escapeValue: false },
+      }),
+      text: this.getTextBody("booking_reminder_title"),
+    };
+  }
+
+  async getHtml(calEvent: CalendarEvent, attendee: Person) {
+    return await renderEmail("AttendeeScheduledEmail", {
+      calEvent,
+      attendee,
+      title: "booking_reminder_title",
+    });
+  }
+}

+import type { CalendarEvent, Person } from "@calcom/types/Calendar";
+import type { TFunction } from "i18next";
+import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
+import AttendeeBookingReminderEmail from "./attendee-booking-reminder-email";
+import OrganizerBookingReminderEmail from "./organizer-booking-reminder-email";
+
+const t = ((key: string, vars?: Record<string, unknown>) =>
+  key === "booking_reminder_subject" ? `Reminder: ${vars?.title} at ${vars?.date}` : key) as TFunction;
+
+const person = (name: string, email: string): Person => ({
+  name,
+  email,
+  timeZone: "UTC",
+  language: { translate: t, locale: "en" },
+});
+
+const organizer = person("Host", "host@example.com");
+const attendee = person("Guest", "guest@example.com");
+
+const calEvent = {
+  type: "intro",
+  title: "Intro call",
+  startTime: "2026-10-10T15:00:00.000Z",
+  endTime: "2026-10-10T15:30:00.000Z",
+  organizer,
+  attendees: [attendee],
+} as CalendarEvent;
+
+class TestAttendeeReminder extends AttendeeBookingReminderEmail {
+  getPayload() {
+    return this.getNodeMailerPayload();
+  }
+}
+
+class TestOrganizerReminder extends OrganizerBookingReminderEmail {
+  getPayload() {
+    return this.getNodeMailerPayload();
+  }
+}
+
+describe("booking reminder emails", () => {
+  it("sends the attendee a reminder without re-attaching the calendar invite", async () => {
+    const payload = await new TestAttendeeReminder(calEvent, attendee).getPayload();
+
+    expect(payload.to).toBe("Guest <guest@example.com>");
+    expect(payload.subject).toMatch(/^Reminder: Intro call at 3:00pm - 3:30pm, saturday, october 10, 2026$/);
+    expect(payload.icalEvent).toBeUndefined();
+    expect(payload.html).toContain("booking_reminder_title");
+    expect(payload.text).toContain("booking_reminder_title");
+  });
+
+  it("sends the host a reminder without re-attaching the calendar invite", async () => {
+    const payload = await new TestOrganizerReminder({ calEvent }).getPayload();
+
+    expect(payload.to).toBe("host@example.com");
+    expect(payload.subject).toMatch(/^Reminder: Intro call at /);
+    expect(payload.icalEvent).toBeUndefined();
+    expect(payload.html).toContain("booking_reminder_title");
+  });
+});

+import prismaMock from "@calcom/testing/lib/__mocks__/prisma";
+import { cancelNoShowTasksForBooking } from "@calcom/features/webhooks/lib/scheduleTrigger";
+import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
+import { BOOKING_REMINDER_LEAD_TIME_MS, scheduleBookingReminderEmail } from "./scheduleBookingReminderEmail";
+
+const HOUR_MS = 60 * 60 * 1000;
+
+const findReminderTasks = (referenceUid: string) =>
+  prismaMock.task.findMany({ where: { type: "sendBookingReminderEmail", referenceUid } });
+
+describe("scheduleBookingReminderEmail", () => {
+  it("schedules the reminder exactly 24 hours before the start time", async () => {
+    const startTime = new Date(Date.now() + 72 * HOUR_MS);
+
+    await scheduleBookingReminderEmail({ id: 1, uid: "booking-uid", startTime });
+
+    const tasks = await findReminderTasks("booking-uid");
+    expect(tasks).toHaveLength(1);
+    expect(tasks[0].scheduledAt.getTime()).toBe(startTime.getTime() - BOOKING_REMINDER_LEAD_TIME_MS);
+    expect(BOOKING_REMINDER_LEAD_TIME_MS).toBe(24 * HOUR_MS);
+    expect(JSON.parse(tasks[0].payload)).toEqual({ bookingId: 1, startTime: startTime.toISOString() });
+  });
+
+  it("does not schedule a reminder when the booking starts less than 24 hours from now", async () => {
+    await scheduleBookingReminderEmail({
+      id: 2,
+      uid: "soon-booking-uid",
+      startTime: new Date(Date.now() + 23 * HOUR_MS),
+    });
+
+    expect(await findReminderTasks("soon-booking-uid")).toHaveLength(0);
+  });
+
+  it("is removed by the cleanup that runs when a booking is cancelled or rescheduled", async () => {
+    await scheduleBookingReminderEmail({
+      id: 3,
+      uid: "cancelled-booking-uid",
+      startTime: new Date(Date.now() + 48 * HOUR_MS),
+    });
+    expect(await findReminderTasks("cancelled-booking-uid")).toHaveLength(1);
+
+    await cancelNoShowTasksForBooking({ bookingUid: "cancelled-booking-uid" });
+
+    expect(await findReminderTasks("cancelled-booking-uid")).toHaveLength(0);
+  });
+});

@@ -0,0 +1,18 @@
+import tasker from "@calcom/features/tasker";
+
+export const BOOKING_REMINDER_LEAD_TIME_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
+
+/**
+ * Keyed on the booking uid so the existing cancel/reschedule cleanup
+ * (`cancelNoShowTasksForBooking`, which deletes every task for that uid) removes it too.
+ */
+export async function scheduleBookingReminderEmail(booking: { id: number; uid: string; startTime: Date }) {
+  const scheduledAt = new Date(booking.startTime.getTime() - BOOKING_REMINDER_LEAD_TIME_MS);
+  if (scheduledAt <= new Date()) return;
+
+  await tasker.create(
+    "sendBookingReminderEmail",
+    { bookingId: booking.id, startTime: booking.startTime.toISOString() },
+    { scheduledAt, referenceUid: booking.uid }
+  );
+}

+import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
+import { sendBookingReminderEmail } from "./sendBookingReminderEmail";
+
+vi.mock("@calcom/emails/email-manager", () => ({
+  sendBookingReminderEmails: vi.fn(),
+}));
+
+vi.mock("@calcom/features/bookings/lib/payment/getBooking", () => ({
+  getBooking: vi.fn(),
+}));
+
+const scheduledStart = new Date("2026-10-10T15:00:00.000Z");
+const evt = { title: "Intro call" };
+const eventType = { metadata: { disableStandardEmails: undefined } };
+
+function mockBooking(booking: { status: BookingStatus; startTime: Date }) {
+  vi.mocked(getBooking).mockResolvedValue({ booking, evt, eventType } as unknown as Awaited<
+    ReturnType<typeof getBooking>
+  >);
+}
+
+const payload = JSON.stringify({ bookingId: 42, startTime: scheduledStart.toISOString() });
+
+describe("sendBookingReminderEmail task", () => {
+  beforeEach(() => {
+    vi.clearAllMocks();
+  });
+
+  it("emails the host and attendees when the booking is still accepted at the scheduled time", async () => {
+    mockBooking({ status: BookingStatus.ACCEPTED, startTime: scheduledStart });
+
+    await sendBookingReminderEmail(payload);
+
+    expect(getBooking).toHaveBeenCalledWith(42);
+    expect(sendBookingReminderEmails).toHaveBeenCalledWith(evt, eventType.metadata);
+  });
+
+  it("does not send when the booking was cancelled", async () => {
+    mockBooking({ status: BookingStatus.CANCELLED, startTime: scheduledStart });
+
+    await sendBookingReminderEmail(payload);
+
+    expect(sendBookingReminderEmails).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+
+  it("does not send when the booking was moved to a different time", async () => {
+    mockBooking({ status: BookingStatus.ACCEPTED, startTime: new Date("2026-10-11T15:00:00.000Z") });
+
+    await sendBookingReminderEmail(payload);
+
+    expect(sendBookingReminderEmails).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+
+  it("rejects malformed payloads", async () => {
+    await expect(sendBookingReminderEmail(JSON.stringify({ bookingId: "nope" }))).rejects.toThrow();
+    expect(getBooking).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+});

+import { sendBookingReminderEmails } from "@calcom/emails/email-manager";
+import { getBooking } from "@calcom/features/bookings/lib/payment/getBooking";
+import logger from "@calcom/lib/logger";
+import { BookingStatus } from "@calcom/prisma/enums";
+import { z } from "zod";
+
+const log = logger.getSubLogger({ prefix: ["sendBookingReminderEmail"] });
+
+export const sendBookingReminderEmailPayloadSchema = z.object({
+  bookingId: z.number(),
+  startTime: z.string(),
+});
+
+export async function sendBookingReminderEmail(payload: string): Promise<void> {
+  const { bookingId, startTime } = sendBookingReminderEmailPayloadSchema.parse(JSON.parse(payload));
+
+  const { booking, evt, eventType } = await getBooking(bookingId);
+
+  // Cancel/reschedule flows delete this task, but re-check so a stale task never reminds about the wrong time
+  if (booking.status !== BookingStatus.ACCEPTED || booking.startTime.toISOString() !== startTime) {
+    log.debug(`Skipping reminder for booking ${bookingId}: no longer accepted at ${startTime}`);
+    return;
+  }
+
+  await sendBookingReminderEmails(evt, eventType.metadata);
+}

3	import { Prisma } from "@calcom/prisma/client";
4	
5	import { type TaskTypes } from "./tasker";
6	
7	const whereSucceeded: Prisma.TaskWhereInput = {
8	  succeededAt: { not: null },
9	};
10	
11	const whereMaxAttemptsReached: Prisma.TaskWhereInput = {
12	  attempts: {
13	    equals: {
14	      // @ts-expect-error prisma is tripping: '_ref' does not exist in type 'FieldRef<"Task", "Int">'
15	      _ref: "maxAttempts",
16	      _container: "Task",
17	    },
18	  },
19	};
20	
21	/** This is a function to ensure new Date is always fresh */
22	const makeWhereUpcomingTasks = (): Prisma.TaskWhereInput => ({
23	  // Get only tasks that have not succeeded yet
24	  succeededAt: null,
25	  // Get only tasks that are scheduled to run now or in the past
26	  scheduledAt: {
27	    lt: new Date(),
28	  },
29	  // Get only tasks where maxAttemps has not been reached
30	  attempts: {
31	    lt: {
32	      // @ts-expect-error prisma is tripping: '_ref' does not exist in type 'FieldRef<"Task", "Int">'
33	      _ref: "maxAttempts",
34	      _container: "Task",
35	    },
36	  },
37	});
38	
39	type Dependencies = {
40	  prismaClient: PrismaClient;
41	};
42	
43	export class TaskRepository {
44	  constructor(private readonly deps: Dependencies) {}
45	
46	  async create(
47	    type: TaskTypes,
48	    payload: string,
49	    options: { scheduledAt?: Date; maxAttempts?: number; referenceUid?: string } = {}
50	  ) {
51	    const { scheduledAt, maxAttempts, referenceUid } = options;
52	    console.info("Creating task", { type, payload, scheduledAt, maxAttempts });
53	    const newTask = await this.deps.prismaClient.task.create({
54	      data: {
55	        payload,
56	        type,
57	        scheduledAt,
58	        maxAttempts,
59	        referenceUid,
60	      },
61	    });
62	    return newTask.id;
63	  }
64	
65	  async getNextBatch() {
66	    console.info("Getting next batch of tasks", makeWhereUpcomingTasks());
67	    return this.deps.prismaClient.task.findMany({
68	      where: makeWhereUpcomingTasks(),
69	      orderBy: {
70	        scheduledAt: "asc",
71	      },
72	      take: 1000,
73	    });
74	  }
75	
76	  async getFailed() {
77	    return this.deps.prismaClient.task.findMany({
78	      where: whereMaxAttemptsReached,
79	    });
80	  }
81	
82	  async getSucceeded() {
83	    return this.deps.prismaClient.task.findMany({
84	      where: whereSucceeded,
85	    });
86	  }
87	
88	  async count() {
89	    return this.deps.prismaClient.task.count();
90	  }
91	
92	  async countUpcoming() {
93	    return this.deps.prismaClient.task.count({
94	      where: makeWhereUpcomingTasks(),
95	    });
96	  }
97	
98	  async countFailed() {
99	    return this.deps.prismaClient.task.count({
100	      where: whereMaxAttemptsReached,
101	    });
102	  }
103	
104	  async countSucceeded() {
105	    return this.deps.prismaClient.task.count({
106	      where: whereSucceeded,
107	    });
108	  }
109	
110	  async retry({
111	    taskId,
112	    lastError,
113	    minRetryIntervalMins,
114	  }: {
115	    taskId: string;
116	    lastError?: string;
117	    minRetryIntervalMins?: number | null;
118	  }) {
119	    const failedAttemptTime = new Date();
120	    const updatedScheduledAt = minRetryIntervalMins
121	      ? new Date(failedAttemptTime.getTime() + 1000 * 60 * minRetryIntervalMins)
122	      : undefined;
123	
124	    return this.deps.prismaClient.task.update({
125	      where: {
126	        id: taskId,
127	      },
128	      data: {
129	        attempts: { increment: 1 },
130	        lastError,
131	        lastFailedAttemptAt: failedAttemptTime,
132	        ...(updatedScheduledAt && {
133	          scheduledAt: updatedScheduledAt,
134	        }),
135	      },
136	    });
137	  }
138	
139	  async succeed(taskId: string) {
140	    return this.deps.prismaClient.task.update({
141	      where: {
142	        id: taskId,
143	      },
144	      data: {
145	        attempts: { increment: 1 },
146	        succeededAt: new Date(),
147	      },
148	    });
149	  }
150	
151	  /**
152	   * Update the payload of a task
153	   *
154	   * @param taskId - The ID of the task to update
155	   * @param newPayload - The new payload string
156	   */
157	  async updatePayload(taskId: string, newPayload: string) {
158	    return this.deps.prismaClient.task.update({
159	      where: {
160	        id: taskId,
161	      },
162	      data: {
163	        payload: newPayload,
164	      },
165	    });
166	  }
167	
168	  async cancel(taskId: string) {
169	    return this.deps.prismaClient.task.delete({
170	      where: {
171	        id: taskId,
172	      },
173	    });
174	  }
175	
176	  async cancelWithReference(referenceUid: string, type: TaskTypes): Promise<{ id: string } | null> {
177	    // prismaClient.task.delete throws an error if the task does not exist, so we catch it and return null
178	    try {
179	      return await this.deps.prismaClient.task.delete({
180	        where: {
181	          referenceUid_type: {
182	            referenceUid,
183	            type,
184	          },
185	        },
186	        select: {
187	          id: true,
188	        },
189	      });
190	    } catch (error) {
191	      if (error instanceof Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError && error.code === "P2025") {
192	        // P2025 is the error code for "Record to delete does not exist"
193	        console.warn(`Task with reference ${referenceUid} and type ${type} does not exist. No action taken.`);
194	        return null;
195	      }
196	      throw error;
197	    }
198	  }
199	
200	  async cleanup() {
201	    // TODO: Uncomment this later
202	    // return this.deps.prismaClient.task.deleteMany({
203	    //   where: {
204	    //     OR: [
205	    //       // Get tasks that have succeeded
206	    //       whereSucceeded,
207	    //       // Get tasks where maxAttemps has been reached
208	    //       whereMaxAttemptsReached,
209	    //     ],
210	    //   },
211	    // });
212	  }
213	
214	}
215	
216	// Export singleton instance for backward compatibility
217	// This allows existing code using Task.create(), Task.succeed(), etc. to continue working
218	export const Task = new TaskRepository({ prismaClient: prisma });

3	import { Task } from "./repository";
4	import type { TaskTypes } from "./tasker";
5	import { type TaskerCreate, type Tasker } from "./tasker";
6	
7	/**
8	 * This is the default internal Tasker that uses the Task repository to create tasks.
9	 * It doesn't have any external dependencies and is suitable for most use cases.
10	 * To use a different Tasker, you can create a new class that implements the Tasker interface.
11	 * Then, you can use the TaskerFactory to select the new Tasker.
12	 */
13	export class InternalTasker implements Tasker {
14	  create: TaskerCreate = async (type, payload, options = {}): Promise<string> => {
15	    const payloadString = typeof payload === "string" ? payload : JSON.stringify(payload);
16	    return Task.create(type, payloadString, options);
17	  };
18	
19	  async cleanup(): Promise<void> {
20	    const count = await Task.cleanup();
21	    logger.info(`Cleaned up ${count} tasks`);
22	  }
23	
24	  async cancel(id: string): Promise<string> {
25	    const task = await Task.cancel(id);
26	    return task.id;
27	  }
28	
29	  async cancelWithReference(referenceUid: string, type: TaskTypes): Promise<string | null> {
30	    const task = await Task.cancelWithReference(referenceUid, type);
31	    return task?.id ?? null;
32	  }
33	}

1	import { Task } from "./repository";
2	import tasksMap, { tasksConfig } from "./tasks";
3	
4	/**
5	 * TaskProcessor handles the processing of tasks from the queue.
6	 * This is separated from task creation to avoid importing all task handlers
7	 * when only creating tasks, which eliminates compilation overhead.
8	 */
9	export class TaskProcessor {
10	  async processQueue(): Promise<void> {
11	    const tasks = await Task.getNextBatch();
12	    console.info(`Processing ${tasks.length} tasks`, tasks);
13	
14	    const tasksPromises = tasks.map(async (task) => {
15	      console.info(
16	        `Processing task ${task.id}, attempt:${task.attempts} maxAttempts:${task.maxAttempts} lastFailedAttempt:${task.lastFailedAttemptAt}`,
17	        task
18	      );
19	      const taskHandlerGetter = tasksMap[task.type as keyof typeof tasksMap];
20	      if (!taskHandlerGetter) throw new Error(`Task handler not found for type ${task.type}`);
21	      const taskConfig = tasksConfig[task.type as keyof typeof tasksConfig];
22	      const taskHandler = await taskHandlerGetter();
23	      return taskHandler(task.payload, task.id)
24	        .then(async () => {
25	          await Task.succeed(task.id);
26	        })
27	        .catch(async (error) => {
28	          console.info(`Retrying task ${task.id}: ${error}`);
29	          await Task.retry({
30	            taskId: task.id,
31	            lastError: error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Unknown error",
32	            minRetryIntervalMins:
33	              taskConfig && "minRetryIntervalMins" in taskConfig ? taskConfig.minRetryIntervalMins : null,
34	          });
35	        });
36	    });
37	    const settled = await Promise.allSettled(tasksPromises);
38	    const failed = settled.filter((result) => result.status === "rejected");
39	    const succeded = settled.filter((result) => result.status === "fulfilled");
40	    console.info({ failed, succeded });
41	  }
42	}

# PR review guide: 24-hour booking reminder emails (commit ef5b32963d, Issue #66)

This is an explanation for reviewing the PR. No code changes are planned.

## 1. Overview: the systems involved

The PR adds no new infrastructure. It connects four systems that already exist:

| System | Where | Role in this PR |
|---|---|---|
| **Booking creation / confirmation** | `RegularBookingService.ts`, `handleConfirmation.ts` | The point where a booking becomes `ACCEPTED`, so the reminder gets scheduled here |
| **Tasker (DB-backed job queue)** | `packages/features/tasker/*` | Stores a `Task` row with a `scheduledAt` time. A cron route (`tasker/api/cron.ts` → `TaskProcessor.processQueue()`) picks up tasks whose `scheduledAt < now` and runs the handler registered for that `type`. Failed tasks are retried until `maxAttempts`. |
| **No-show task cleanup** | `webhooks/lib/scheduleTrigger.ts → cancelNoShowTasksForBooking` | When it's called with only a `bookingUid`, it runs `prisma.task.deleteMany({ where: { referenceUid } })`, which deletes **every** task tied to that booking uid. Cancel (`handleCancelBooking.ts:490`), reschedule (`RegularBookingService.ts:2419`) and host "request reschedule" (`requestReschedule.handler.ts:101`) already call it. |
| **Email manager + templates** | `packages/emails` | Builds and sends the emails. Most of the new templates reuse the existing "scheduled" email layout. |

### End-to-end flow

```
Booking confirmed (instantly, or later by the host approving it)
  └─ scheduleBookingReminderEmail(booking)
       └─ tasker.create("sendBookingReminderEmail",
                        {bookingId, startTime}, {scheduledAt: start-24h, referenceUid: booking.uid})
                 │
     ┌───────────┴──────────────────────────────┐
     │ Cancel / reschedule happens first?        │
     │  → cancelNoShowTasksForBooking(uid)       │
     │    deletes the Task row (reminder is gone)│
     └───────────────────────────────────────────┘
                 │ (otherwise)
Cron tick after scheduledAt → TaskProcessor → tasks["sendBookingReminderEmail"]
  └─ sendBookingReminderEmail(payload)
       ├─ getBooking(bookingId)  (rebuilds the CalendarEvent from the DB)
       ├─ guard: status === ACCEPTED && startTime unchanged, otherwise skip
       └─ sendBookingReminderEmails(evt, metadata)
            ├─ OrganizerBookingReminderEmail → host (and any team members in evt.team)
            └─ AttendeeBookingReminderEmail  → each attendee
```

**How rescheduling works:** in Cal.diy, a reschedule creates a **new booking with a new uid**. The original booking's tasks get deleted by the cleanup above, and the new booking runs through `RegularBookingService` again, which schedules a fresh reminder for the new time. So the "update the reminder" requirement in AC #3 is handled as a delete followed by a create. Nothing ever edits an existing task.

---

## 2. File-by-file walkthrough

### Scheduling side

#### `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/scheduleBookingReminderEmail.ts` (new)
- **`BOOKING_REMINDER_LEAD_TIME_MS`**: the constant 24h in milliseconds. It's exported so the test can assert against it.
- **`scheduleBookingReminderEmail(booking: {id, uid, startTime})`**
  - Computes `scheduledAt = startTime − 24h`.
  - **Early return if `scheduledAt <= now`.** This covers AC #1 ("booked at least 24h in advance") and the PR's design decision that a booking moved to under 24h away gets no reminder.
  - Calls `tasker.create("sendBookingReminderEmail", { bookingId, startTime: ISO }, { scheduledAt, referenceUid: booking.uid })`.
  - Using `referenceUid = booking.uid` is the key design choice. It's what lets the existing cleanup delete the reminder without any new cleanup code.
  - The payload includes `startTime` so the handler can tell later if the booking was moved (see the guard below).
- Relationships: called by `RegularBookingService` and `handleConfirmation`. Creates tasks that `sendBookingReminderEmail` consumes.

#### `packages/features/bookings/lib/service/RegularBookingService.ts` (modified)
- The new `try` block (~line 2553) runs `scheduleBookingReminderEmail(booking)` when `isConfirmedByDefault && !isDryRun`. This is the path for bookings that need no approval, and that includes the new booking created by a reschedule.
- Errors are logged rather than thrown, so a failure to schedule a reminder never breaks the booking itself. This matches the `scheduleNoShowTriggers` block right above it.
- The other changes in this file are noise: the `isRescheduleReasonRequired` import was moved (alphabetical order) and one call was re-wrapped. There's no behavior change.

#### `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleConfirmation.ts` (modified)
- This runs when a host **approves** a booking that required confirmation. Those bookings skip the `isConfirmedByDefault` branch above, so they need their own scheduling call.
- It calls `scheduleBookingReminderEmail` for every booking in `updatedBookings`. For recurring series, that's one reminder per occurrence. It uses `Promise.allSettled` and logs each failure.
- `updatedBookings` already selects `id`, `uid` and `startTime` (lines ~230/287), so the call type-checks.

### Tasker registration

#### `packages/features/tasker/tasker.ts` (modified)
- Adds `sendBookingReminderEmail` to the `TaskPayloads` type map. That makes `"sendBookingReminderEmail"` a valid `TaskTypes` value and gives `tasker.create(...)` a typed payload. The payload type is inferred from the zod schema in the task file.

#### `packages/features/tasker/tasks/index.ts` (modified)
- Registers a lazy `import()` for the handler in the `tasks` map. `TaskProcessor` looks up handlers by `task.type`, so without this entry the cron would throw "Task handler not found".

#### `packages/features/tasker/tasks/sendBookingReminderEmail.ts` (new)
- **`sendBookingReminderEmailPayloadSchema`**: zod schema `{ bookingId: number, startTime: string }`. It's used for both runtime validation and the type in `tasker.ts`.
- **`sendBookingReminderEmail(payload: string)`**: the task handler.
  1. Parses and validates the JSON payload. A bad payload throws, and the processor then retries the task.
  2. `getBooking(bookingId)` (an existing helper from the payment flow) rebuilds the booking, a `CalendarEvent` (`evt`) with translated organizer and attendees, and `eventType.metadata`.
  3. **Guard:** it skips the send unless `status === ACCEPTED` **and** the stored `startTime` still matches the payload. This is a backstop in case the delete-based cleanup missed something (for example a cancel path that doesn't call `cancelNoShowTasksForBooking`).
  4. Calls `sendBookingReminderEmails(evt, eventType.metadata)`.

### Email side

#### `packages/emails/email-manager.ts` (modified)
- **`sendBookingReminderEmails(calEvent, eventTypeMetadata?)`**: follows the same shape as the existing `sendScheduledEmailsAndSMS`-style functions.
  - `formatCalEvent` normalizes the event.
  - **Host emails** are sent unless `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(metadata)`: one to the organizer, plus one per `team.members` entry.
  - **Attendee emails** are sent unless `shouldSkipAttendeeEmailWithSettings(metadata)`: one per attendee, with `additionalNotes` stripped when `hideCalendarNotes` is set.
  - Every send is wrapped in `sendEmail(() => new Template(...))` and awaited with `Promise.all`.
- This answers one of the issue's open questions: **hosts get reminders by default**, and the existing "disable host emails" event-type setting turns them off.
- The import reshuffle at the top of the file (lodash/zod moved down) is formatter noise.

#### `packages/emails/templates/attendee-booking-reminder-email.ts` (new)
- **`AttendeeBookingReminderEmail extends AttendeeScheduledEmail`**: reuses the confirmation email's body, which already covers the details AC #2 asks for: time in the recipient's own timezone, location/video link, and reschedule/cancel links.
  - **`getNodeMailerPayload()`** overrides the parent's payload:
    - `icalEvent: undefined`, so no `.ics` file is re-attached. Re-attaching it would show up as a calendar update in the recipient's client.
    - `subject` uses the new `booking_reminder_subject` translation key.
    - `text` uses the plain-text body with the `booking_reminder_title` heading.
  - **`getHtml()`** renders the existing `AttendeeScheduledEmail` React template with `title: "booking_reminder_title"`.

#### `packages/emails/templates/organizer-booking-reminder-email.ts` (new)
- **`OrganizerBookingReminderEmail extends OrganizerScheduledEmail`**: the host-side version of the class above, with the same overrides. `getHtml` also passes `teamMember`, so team-member copies go to the right person.

#### `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json` (modified)
- `booking_reminder_subject`: "Reminder: {{title}} at {{date}}"
- `booking_reminder_title`: "Your event starts in 24 hours"

### Tests

- **`emails/templates/booking-reminder-email.test.ts`**: uses small test subclasses to expose the protected `getNodeMailerPayload`. Checks the recipient, the subject format, that there's no `icalEvent`, and that the reminder title appears in the html and text.
- **`handleNewBooking/scheduleBookingReminderEmail.test.ts`**: runs against the in-memory `prismaMock`. Checks that:
  - the task is scheduled at exactly start − 24h with the right payload;
  - nothing is scheduled when the booking is under 24h away;
  - `cancelNoShowTasksForBooking` deletes the reminder (the cancel/reschedule cleanup).
- **`tasker/tasks/sendBookingReminderEmail.test.ts`**: mocks `getBooking` and the email manager. Checks that the email sends when the booking is ACCEPTED at the same time, is skipped when CANCELLED or moved, and that a malformed payload throws.

---

## 3. Points worth raising in review

1. **Cleanup depends on a side effect.** Reminder deletion only works because `cancelNoShowTasksForBooking` (named after no-show tasks) deletes *every* task for the uid when `triggerEvent` isn't passed. If someone later narrows that function to only delete no-show tasks, reminders would stop being deleted. The handler's status/startTime guard would still stop wrong emails, but it's worth discussing, or at least noting in a comment where `cancelNoShowTasksForBooking` is defined.
2. **The reschedule cleanup sits inside `if (isConfirmedByDefault)`** (RegularBookingService ~2403–2423). For a reschedule that needs confirmation, the original booking's tasks aren't deleted at that point. Confirm the expected behavior: the original's reminder still fires only if the original is still ACCEPTED at the old time.
3. **Team members won't actually get emails.** `getBooking` builds `team.members: []`, so the team-member loop in `sendBookingReminderEmails` never runs in practice. For collective or round-robin events, only the organizer and attendees get the reminder.
4. **"Exactly 24h" really means the next cron tick after start − 24h.** The precision depends on how often `tasker/api/cron.ts` runs. The tests check `scheduledAt`, not when the email is actually delivered.
5. **Deleted bookings retry.** If the booking is gone, `getBooking` throws `HttpCode 204` and the task retries until `maxAttempts` instead of quietly succeeding. This is minor.
6. **Duplicate scheduling throws.** `Task` has a unique constraint on `(referenceUid, type)`, so scheduling twice for the same uid throws. Today that error is caught and logged, and the two scheduling paths shouldn't both run for the same booking.
7. **Diff noise.** The import reorders in `email-manager.ts` and `RegularBookingService.ts` plus the line re-wrap don't change behavior. They could be dropped to keep the diff focused.
8. **The PR description's "rescheduled to under 24h → no email" decision** is implemented by the early return in `scheduleBookingReminderEmail`, which matches the stated design.

## Verification (if you want to run it yourself)
- `TZ=UTC yarn vitest run packages/emails/templates/booking-reminder-email.test.ts packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/scheduleBookingReminderEmail.test.ts packages/features/tasker/tasks/sendBookingReminderEmail.test.ts`

I read commit `ef5b32963d` ("Add 24 hour email reminders" by lexzach) and the code around it. I haven't run the tests.

## How it works

The PR adds no new infrastructure. It connects four systems the codebase already has:

1. **Where bookings get confirmed.** `RegularBookingService.ts` handles bookings that are accepted straight away, and `handleConfirmation.ts` handles the ones a host approves later. The reminder is scheduled from both.
2. **The tasker, a job queue stored in the database.** `tasker.create(type, payload, { scheduledAt, referenceUid })` writes a row to the `Task` table. A cron route (`tasker/api/cron.ts` → `TaskProcessor.processQueue()`) picks up tasks whose `scheduledAt` has passed, runs the handler registered for that type, and retries failures until `maxAttempts`.
3. **The existing no-show task cleanup.** When `cancelNoShowTasksForBooking({ bookingUid })` is called without a `triggerEvent`, it deletes **every** task whose `referenceUid` matches that booking (`scheduleTrigger.ts:614`). Three places already call it:
   - cancel (`handleCancelBooking.ts:490`)
   - reschedule (`RegularBookingService.ts:2419`)
   - a host requesting a reschedule (`requestReschedule.handler.ts:101`)
4. **The email manager and templates.** The new reminder emails reuse the existing "booking scheduled" templates.

**The full flow:**
1. A booking is confirmed, which calls `scheduleBookingReminderEmail`.
2. That creates a task set to run at start time minus 24h, tagged with `referenceUid = booking.uid`.
3. If the booking is cancelled or rescheduled first, the existing cleanup deletes the task.
4. Otherwise the cron runs the handler, which reloads the booking, checks it's still valid, and sends the emails.

**Rescheduling:** a reschedule creates a *new* booking with a new uid. The old booking's tasks get deleted, and the new booking schedules its own reminder. So "updating" a reminder (acceptance criterion 3) is really delete-then-create.

## File by file

### Scheduling

**`handleNewBooking/scheduleBookingReminderEmail.ts` (new)**
- `BOOKING_REMINDER_LEAD_TIME_MS` is 24 hours in milliseconds. It's exported so the tests can use it.
- `scheduleBookingReminderEmail({ id, uid, startTime })`:
  - Works out `scheduledAt = startTime − 24h`.
  - Returns early if that time has already passed. This is how "booked at least 24h ahead" is enforced, and also the PR's decision that a booking moved to under 24h away gets no reminder.
  - Otherwise it creates a task with payload `{ bookingId, startTime }`.
- Tagging the task with the booking's uid is the key choice: it lets the existing cleanup delete it with no new code. The `startTime` in the payload lets the handler notice later if the booking was moved.

**`RegularBookingService.ts`**
- A new `try` block (around line 2553) calls `scheduleBookingReminderEmail(booking)` when `isConfirmedByDefault && !isDryRun`.
- Errors are logged, not thrown, so a scheduling failure never breaks the booking. This matches the `scheduleNoShowTriggers` block just above it.
- The moved `isRescheduleReasonRequired` import and one re-wrapped line are formatting only.

**`handleConfirmation.ts`**
- This covers bookings that need host approval, which skip the path above.
- When the host approves, it calls `scheduleBookingReminderEmail` for each booking in `updatedBookings`. A recurring series gets one reminder per occurrence.
- It uses `Promise.allSettled` and logs each failure.

### Registering the task

**`tasker/tasker.ts`**
- Adds `sendBookingReminderEmail` to the `TaskPayloads` type map. This makes it a valid task type and gives `tasker.create(...)` a typed payload, inferred from the zod schema.

**`tasker/tasks/index.ts`**
- Registers the handler as a lazy import. The processor looks handlers up by `task.type`; without this entry the cron would throw "Task handler not found".

**`tasker/tasks/sendBookingReminderEmail.ts` (new)**
- `sendBookingReminderEmailPayloadSchema` is the zod schema `{ bookingId: number, startTime: string }`, used both to check the payload at runtime and for the type above.
- `sendBookingReminderEmail(payload)` is the handler:
  1. It parses and validates the payload. A bad payload throws, so the processor retries it.
  2. It calls the existing `getBooking(bookingId)` helper (from the payment flow) to rebuild the calendar event (`evt`), with translated organizer and attendee details, plus the event type's metadata.
  3. **Guard:** it skips sending unless the booking's status is still `ACCEPTED` *and* its start time still matches the payload. This is a backstop in case the cleanup missed the task.
  4. It calls `sendBookingReminderEmails(evt, metadata)`.

### Emails

**`email-manager.ts`**
- `sendBookingReminderEmails(calEvent, metadata)` follows the same pattern as the other send functions:
  - It normalizes the event with `formatCalEvent`.
  - **Host emails** are sent unless the event type disables host emails (`eventTypeDisableHostEmail`). That's one to the organizer plus one per team member.
  - **Attendee emails** are sent unless `shouldSkipAttendeeEmailWithSettings` says to skip them. That's one per attendee, with notes removed if `hideCalendarNotes` is set.
  - It sends everything with `Promise.all`.
- This answers one of the issue's open questions: hosts get the reminder by default.
- The lodash/zod imports moving lower in the file is formatter noise.

**`templates/attendee-booking-reminder-email.ts` and `templates/organizer-booking-reminder-email.ts` (new)**
- Each extends the matching existing "scheduled" email class, so it inherits the body acceptance criterion 2 asks for: the time in the recipient's timezone, the location or video link, and reschedule/cancel links.
- `getNodeMailerPayload()` overrides three fields:
  - `icalEvent: undefined`, so the calendar invite isn't re-attached. Re-attaching it would show up as a calendar update.
  - The subject uses the new reminder subject string.
  - The plain-text body uses the new reminder heading.
- `getHtml()` renders the existing React template with the reminder heading. The organizer version also passes `teamMember`.

**`i18n/locales/en/common.json`**
- `booking_reminder_subject`: "Reminder: {{title}} at {{date}}"
- `booking_reminder_title`: "Your event starts in 24 hours"

### Tests
- **Template test:** small subclasses expose the protected payload method. It checks the recipient, the subject format, that no invite is attached, and that the reminder heading appears.
- **Scheduling test:** runs against the in-memory Prisma mock. It checks that:
  - the task is set for exactly start − 24h with the right payload;
  - nothing is scheduled when the booking is under 24h away;

## Things worth raising in the review

1. **Cleanup depends on a side effect.** Reminders only get deleted because a function named for *no-show* tasks deletes every task for the booking. If someone later narrows it, reminders stop being cleaned up. The handler's guard would still stop wrong emails going out, but it's worth a comment or a dedicated cancel call.
2. **Some reschedules don't run the cleanup.** In `RegularBookingService` (~2403–2423) the cleanup sits inside `if (isConfirmedByDefault)`. When a reschedule needs approval, the original booking's tasks aren't deleted at that point. Worth checking what's expected there.
3. **Team members never get the reminder.** `getBooking` builds `team.members: []`, so the team-member loop never runs. For team events, only the organizer and attendees are emailed.
4. **"Exactly 24h" really means the next cron run after that time.** The tests check the scheduled time, not when the email is actually sent.
5. **Deleted bookings cause retries.** If the booking no longer exists, `getBooking` throws and the task retries until `maxAttempts` instead of quietly finishing.
6. **Scheduling twice throws.** The `Task` table has a unique constraint on `(referenceUid, type)`, so a second reminder for the same booking throws. The error is caught and logged, and the two scheduling paths shouldn't overlap.
7. **Diff noise.** The import reorders and the one re-wrapped line in `email-manager.ts` and `RegularBookingService.ts` could be dropped to keep the PR focused.

528:2. **Retry mechanism**: Not all tasks succeed on the first attempt due to errors or external dependencies. 3624	**How it works**
3625	- When a booking is accepted, a job is queued in the app's existing task queue (the `tasker`) to run at start time minus 24 hours. This happens in two places: [RegularBookingService.ts](packages/features/bookings/lib/service/RegularBookingService.ts) covers bookings that don't need approval, and [handleConfirmation.ts](packages/features/bookings/lib/handleConfirmation.ts) covers bookings that were approved, paid for, or are recurring.
3626	- The job is tied to the booking's ID, so the cleanup that already runs on cancel, reschedule and "request reschedule" deletes it. No changes to those flows were needed.
3627	- A reschedule creates a new booking, which gets its own reminder at the new time.
3628	- As a safety net, the job checks the booking again before sending ([sendBookingReminderEmail.ts](packages/features/tasker/tasks/sendBookingReminderEmail.ts)). It only sends if the booking is still accepted at the original start time.
3629	- The emails reuse the existing "event scheduled" layout with a reminder title and subject, and leave off the calendar invite attachment. They respect the event type's settings for turning off host or attendee emails.

| Criterion | Score | Notes |

| **Correctness** | **8** | All four acceptance criteria are covered: the 24h scheduling, host and attendee emails (built on the existing template, which already includes local time, the meeting link and reschedule/cancel links), removal on cancel or reschedule, and tests. There are gaps (below), but the core path is sound. |
| **Test coverage** | **7** | Each new unit is tested, and the tests check behavior rather than just running code. The places where the new code is called from aren't tested (below). |
| **Code quality** | **8** | Small and focused: 7 code files, about 190 lines of non-test code. It reuses the task queue, the existing cleanup, `getBooking` and the existing email templates instead of building new ones. Names are clear, and errors are isolated so a reminder failure can't break a booking. The deductions are formatting churn and the reliance on the no-show cleanup function. |
| **Documentation** | **7** | The inline comments explain *why* (no re-attached invite, uid-keyed cleanup, the stale-task guard), as the project's comment rules ask. The PR description records a clear design decision, but it overstates some things and leaves others out (below). |
| **AI transparency** | **6** | The full AI log is committed, which is good. It shows the agent ran the new tests, the existing booking suites (140 passing), the type check and Biome. But the log has only **one** human message: the initial prompt. Nothing shows the author questioned or changed the AI's output, and the PR description doesn't say AI was used. |
| **Overall** | **7** | Approve once the small fixes below are made. |

## Correctness gaps
- **The team-member emails never go out.** `getBooking` builds `team.members: []`, so the team-member loop in `sendBookingReminderEmails` never runs. For team events, only the organizer and attendees get reminded. Either drop the loop or load the members.
- **Some reschedules don't remove the old reminder.** The cleanup in `RegularBookingService` runs only when `isConfirmedByDefault` is true. For a reschedule that needs host approval, the old booking's reminder isn't deleted at that point. It still won't fire unless the old booking stays accepted at its old time, but this should be confirmed on purpose.
- **"Exactly 24 hours" really means the next cron run after that time.** It's close enough, but the PR doesn't say it depends on `/api/tasks/cron` running.
- **One of the issue's open questions was answered silently.** Hosts get reminders by default. That's a reasonable choice, but the PR should say it was made.

## Test gaps
- Nothing checks that `RegularBookingService` or `handleConfirmation` actually call `scheduleBookingReminderEmail`, or that dry runs and bookings needing approval skip it. If someone deleted those calls, every test would still pass.
- The "cancel/reschedule" test calls `cancelNoShowTasksForBooking` directly instead of going through the cancel or reschedule flow. It proves the cleanup function works, not that the flows trigger it.
- The PR description says the tests "check that the email is delivered exactly 24 hours out", which overstates them. They check the scheduled time on the task and that the handler calls a mocked email function. Nothing runs the cron or `processQueue` end to end.
- The template test only checks that the translation key appears, not the rendered English text. That's acceptable given how the existing templates are tested.

## Code quality nits
- **Formatting churn:** Biome reordered imports in `email-manager.ts` and `RegularBookingService.ts` and re-wrapped one line, none of it related to this feature. Revert it to keep the diff focused.
- **Hidden dependency:** deleting reminders relies on a function named for *no-show* tasks that happens to delete every task for a booking. A comment where that function is defined, or a dedicated cancel call, would protect against someone narrowing it later.
- **Commit message:** "Add 24 hour email reminders" doesn't follow the conventional-commit format the project requires. It should be something like `feat(bookings): send 24h reminder emails`.
- **Commit contents:** the 3,643-line AI log is in the same commit as the code. It doesn't count toward the PR size limit, but a separate commit would make the review easier.

## Documentation
- The description says the reminder is "adjusted" on reschedule. In reality it's deleted and a new one is created for the new booking, which is worth saying plainly.
- Several limits the AI flagged in its own final summary didn't make it into the PR: the new strings are English-only, delivery depends on the cron, and bookings made under 24h ahead get no reminder.
- Small typo: "Rational" should be "Rationale".

## AI transparency
For a higher score, add a short "AI usage & verification" section to the PR. It should say:
- that Claude Code wrote the change (and link the log);
- what the author checked themselves, such as reading the diff, running the tests (your confirmation that the suite passes helps here), or triggering a real reminder locally;
- any decisions the author made rather than the AI, such as sending to hosts by default.

## To merge
1. Fix or remove the team-member loop.
2. Revert the unrelated formatting changes.
3. Use a conventional commit and PR title.
4. Update the PR description: how reschedules actually work, the limits above, and the AI usage note.
5. Optionally, add one test that the booking flow calls the scheduler.

// eslint-disable-next-line no-restricted-imports

import type { CalendarEvent } from "@calcom/types/Calendar";
import { cloneDeep } from "lodash";

// format CalEvent to remove platformClientId from email addresses
const formatClientIdFromEmails = (calEvent: CalendarEvent, clientId: string) => {
  const attendees = calEvent.attendees.map((attendee) => ({
    ...attendee,
    email: attendee.email.replace(`+${clientId}`, ""),
  }));
  const organizer = {
    ...calEvent.organizer,
    email: calEvent.organizer.email.replace(`+${clientId}`, ""),
  };
  return [attendees, organizer];
};

export const formatCalEvent = (calEvent: CalendarEvent) => {
  const clonedEvent = cloneDeep(calEvent);
  if (clonedEvent.platformClientId) {
    const [attendees, organizer] = formatClientIdFromEmails(clonedEvent, clonedEvent.platformClientId);
    Object.assign(clonedEvent, { attendees, organizer });
  }

  return clonedEvent;
};

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-08 14:49:49Z)**_

You found the right loop: `email-manager.ts:592-596`. It runs fine, but it always loops over an empty list, so it sends nothing.

### 1. Lines 83–91 of `getBooking.ts` don't load members

That block is part of the Prisma `select`, which lists the columns read from the database:

```ts
team: {
  select: {
    id: true,
    name: true,
    parentId: true,
    hideBranding: true,
    parent: { select: { hideBranding: true } },
  },
},
```

It asks for the team's `id`, `name`, `parentId` and branding settings. It never asks for the team's members, so none come back from the database.

### 2. The empty list is created later, at lines 197–203

`getBooking` then builds the `evt` object that gets passed to the email code:

```ts
team: booking.eventType?.team
  ? {
      name: booking.eventType.team.name,
      id: booking.eventType.team.id,
      members: [],
    }
  : undefined,
```

`members: []` is an empty array written directly into the code. It's probably there because the `CalendarEvent` type requires a `members` field whenever `team` is set. Since `getBooking` came from the payment flow, which never emailed team members, an empty placeholder was enough there.

### 3. Nothing fills it in on the way to the loop

The value passes through these steps unchanged:

1. `sendBookingReminderEmail.ts` passes `evt` straight to `sendBookingReminderEmails(evt, eventType.metadata)`.
2. `sendBookingReminderEmails` calls `formatCalEvent(calEvent)` (`packages/lib/formatCalendarEvent.ts`). That only deep-copies the event and strips a platform client id from email addresses. It doesn't touch `team`.
3. The loop then runs `for (const teamMember of formattedCalEvent.team?.members ?? [])`:
   - For a personal event, `team` is `undefined`, so `?? []` gives an empty array.
   - For a team event, `team.members` is the `[]` from step 2.

Either way the loop body never runs. The only host email that actually goes out is the organizer one on line 590.

### Why it looks right at first

The loop was copied from the email functions that run when a booking is first made. Those get an `evt` from `RegularBookingService`, where the team members are filled in. The reminder runs a day later from a background task, and its `evt` comes from `getBooking` instead, which leaves the list empty. The unit tests use personal events with no team, so they don't catch it.

### What this means for the review

The bug is limited: on team events (collective or round-robin with several hosts), the other hosts don't get a reminder. The organizer and attendees still do. The author has two options:
- **Remove the loop** and say in the PR that only the organizer gets the host reminder.
- **Load the members.** Either add `members` to the Prisma select and map them into `evt.team.members`, or look them up in the task handler before sending.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-08 14:54:40Z)**_

I checked this one properly, and it turns out to be **not a real bug**. The old reminder isn't deleted, but it can never send. I should have traced it before listing it as a correctness gap.

### What happens on a reschedule that needs approval

Say an attendee reschedules a booking whose event type requires confirmation.

**1. Is the new booking confirmed by default?** No. `getRequiresConfirmationFlags.ts:92` decides this:
```ts
return (!requiresConfirmation && price === 0) || userReschedulingIsOwner;
```
Approval is required and the person rescheduling isn't the host, so `isConfirmedByDefault` is `false`. The new booking is created as `PENDING`.

**2. The original booking is cancelled anyway, in the same transaction.** In `createBooking.ts:253-264`, a reschedule (of a non-seated event) always prepares this update:
```ts
data: { rescheduled: true, status: BookingStatus.CANCELLED, ... }
```
`createBooking.ts:140-141` applies it inside the same `prisma.$transaction` that creates the new booking. This doesn't depend on `isConfirmedByDefault`, so the original becomes `CANCELLED` straight away, even though the host hasn't approved the new time.

**3. The cleanup doesn't run.** The `cancelNoShowTasksForBooking(originalRescheduledBooking.uid)` call at `RegularBookingService.ts:2419` sits inside `if (isConfirmedByDefault)`, so it's skipped. The original booking's reminder row stays in the `Task` table. This is the gap I flagged.

**4. The reminder's own check stops it.** When the cron reaches that leftover task 24h before the *old* time, `sendBookingReminderEmail.ts` reloads the booking and checks:
```ts
if (booking.status !== BookingStatus.ACCEPTED || booking.startTime.toISOString() !== startTime) {
  log.debug(...); return;
}
```
The original is `CANCELLED`, so it returns without sending. The task processor marks the task as succeeded and it's never picked up again.

**5. The new booking's reminder.**
- If the host approves the new booking, `handleConfirmation` calls `scheduleBookingReminderEmail` (the change at `handleConfirmation.ts:380`), and a reminder is scheduled for the new time.
- If the host rejects it, no reminder is ever created for it.

### Summary

| Booking | Status after the reschedule | Reminder task | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Original | `CANCELLED` (step 2) | Not deleted | Runs, sees CANCELLED, sends nothing |
| New | `PENDING`, then `ACCEPTED` if approved | Created when the host approves | Sends at the new time minus 24h |

So acceptance criterion 3 holds for this path too. It's handled by the handler's check rather than by deleting the task, which is exactly the backstop that check's code comment describes.

### Correcting the review
- Move this from "correctness gap" to a **nit**. On this path the leftover task is a harmless dead row. Those rows aren't cleaned up anyway, because `TaskRepository.cleanup()` is commented out with a TODO.
- It's still a reason to keep that check and **not** let anyone remove it later as "redundant", since this path depends on it. A test covering a reschedule that needs approval would make that dependency explicit.
- Seated events are the exception to step 2: the original booking isn't cancelled there (`!evt.seatsPerTimeSlot`). Seated reschedules go through a separate seats flow that I haven't traced. If you want that covered, it's the one remaining path to check.

With this item cleared, I'd raise **Correctness from 8 to 8.5**. The empty team-member list is the only real functional gap left.

I checked the gaps against the actual test files and the test helpers they use. Every gap I listed holds up, and I found one more I'd missed: `sendBookingReminderEmails` itself never runs in any test.

## How I checked
- **Which tests mention the feature at all:** I searched every test and spec file for `scheduleBookingReminderEmail`, `sendBookingReminderEmail`, `BookingReminderEmail` and `booking_reminder`. Only the 3 new test files match. No existing test references the feature.
- **Whether anything tests the cron:** I searched test files for `processQueue` or `TaskProcessor`. Nothing matches, so the queue processor isn't tested anywhere in the repo.
- **Whether existing tests look at tasks:** I searched for `.task.findMany`, `findFirst`, `count` and `referenceUid` in tests. The only task query is in the new scheduling test. The other `referenceUid` hits are about booking seats, not tasks.
- **What `prismaMock` is:** I read `packages/testing/src/lib/__mocks__/prisma.ts`. It's **prismock**, an in-memory fake Prisma that is cleared before every test. It isn't a stub, so code using it really writes and reads rows.

## What each test file does

### 1. `packages/emails/templates/booking-reminder-email.test.ts`
**What it tests:** the two email template classes on their own.
**Setup:**
- A fake translation function `t` returns the key name unchanged, except `booking_reminder_subject`, which it formats as `Reminder: {title} at {date}`.
- One event, "Intro call", on 2026-10-10 at 15:00 UTC, with one host and one guest, both in UTC.
- Small test subclasses expose the protected `getNodeMailerPayload()`, so the test can inspect the email exactly as it would be handed to the mail sender. Nothing is actually sent.

| Test case | What it checks |
|---|---|
| "sends the attendee a reminder without re-attaching the calendar invite" | The email goes to `Guest <guest@example.com>`. The subject matches `Reminder: Intro call at 3:00pm - 3:30pm, saturday, october 10, 2026`, which shows the date is formatted in the recipient's timezone. There's no `.ics` attachment. The HTML and plain-text bodies both contain the `booking_reminder_title` key. |
| "sends the host a reminder without re-attaching the calendar invite" | Same checks for the organizer version: the recipient is `host@example.com`, the subject starts with `Reminder: Intro call at`, there's no attachment, and the HTML contains the reminder title key. |

### 2. `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/scheduleBookingReminderEmail.test.ts`
**What it tests:** the scheduling function, using the **real** tasker and task repository on top of the in-memory database. A helper fetches the `sendBookingReminderEmail` tasks for a given booking uid.

| Test case | What it checks |
|---|---|
| "schedules the reminder exactly 24 hours before the start time" | For a booking 72h away, it calls the scheduler. Exactly one task exists, its `scheduledAt` is the start time minus 24h, the lead-time constant equals 24h, and the payload is `{ bookingId: 1, startTime }`. |
| "does not schedule a reminder when the booking starts less than 24 hours from now" | For a booking 23h away, no task is created, so the early return works. |
| "is removed by the cleanup that runs when a booking is cancelled or rescheduled" | It schedules a reminder for a booking 48h away and confirms it exists. It then calls `cancelNoShowTasksForBooking({ bookingUid })` **directly** and confirms the task is gone. The real `deleteMany` code runs against the in-memory database. |

### 3. `packages/features/tasker/tasks/sendBookingReminderEmail.test.ts`
**What it tests:** the task handler that the cron would run.
**Setup:** `getBooking` and `sendBookingReminderEmails` are both **mocked**. The payload is `{ bookingId: 42, startTime: 2026-10-10T15:00Z }`.

| Test case | What it checks |
|---|---|
| "emails the host and attendees when the booking is still accepted at the scheduled time" | The booking is ACCEPTED with the same start time. It checks that `getBooking(42)` is called and that the mocked `sendBookingReminderEmails` receives the event and metadata. |
| "does not send when the booking was cancelled" | Status CANCELLED, so the email function isn't called. |
| "does not send when the booking was moved to a different time" | Still ACCEPTED, but the start time is a day later, so the email function isn't called. |
| "rejects malformed payloads" | `{ bookingId: "nope" }` makes zod throw, and `getBooking` is never reached. |

## The gaps, checked one by one

| Gap I claimed | Confirmed? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| No test checks that `RegularBookingService` or `handleConfirmation` call the scheduler | **Yes** | Only the 3 new files mention the feature. The existing booking tests (the 140 the AI log says pass) do run `RegularBookingService`, so reminder tasks probably get created along the way, but no test looks for them. Deleting either call would leave every test green. |
| The cancel/reschedule test calls the cleanup directly instead of going through the cancel flow | **Yes** | Test 2.3 imports and calls `cancelNoShowTasksForBooking` itself. Nothing runs `handleCancelBooking` or a reschedule and then checks the task is gone. |
| No end-to-end cron or delivery test | **Yes** | No test anywhere calls `processQueue`. The tests check `scheduledAt` (file 2) and that a mocked email function is called (file 3), but never the task being picked up and actually sent. The PR description's "check that the email is delivered exactly 24 hours out" overstates this. |
| The template test checks translation keys, not rendered text | **Yes** | The fake `t` returns keys unchanged, so the tests assert `html` contains the string `"booking_reminder_title"`, not "Your event starts in 24 hours". |
| The tests only use personal events, so the empty team-member list isn't caught | **Yes** | File 1's event has no `team`, and file 3 mocks the email function away entirely. |

### The gap I missed: `sendBookingReminderEmails` never runs in a test
- File 3 mocks it.
- File 1 builds the template classes directly and never calls it.

So nothing tests the logic inside it:
- the `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` check, which decides whether hosts are emailed;
- the `shouldSkipAttendeeEmailWithSettings` check, which decides whether attendees are emailed;
- the team-member loop;
- removing notes when `hideCalendarNotes` is set.

That's the function that decides **who gets emailed**, so it's the most important untested part.

## Revised test coverage score: 7 → 6.5
Each new piece is tested on its own, and the tests check real behavior: file 2 uses the real tasker and database code, and file 3's guard tests are good. But every link *between* the pieces is either mocked or called by hand, and the deciding-who-gets-emailed logic is never exercised. The most useful additions would be:
1. A test of `sendBookingReminderEmails` with a mocked `sendEmail`, covering the host-disabled and attendee-skip settings.
2. A booking-flow test (the `handleNewBooking/test` suites already have the setup) that books an event 48h out and checks a reminder task exists, then cancels it and checks the task is gone.

```text
import type { NextRequest } from "next/server";
import { NextResponse } from "next/server";

import { TaskProcessor } from "../task-processor";

async function handler(request: NextRequest) {
  const authHeader = request.headers.get("authorization");
  if (authHeader !== `Bearer ${process.env.CRON_SECRET}`) {
    return new Response("Unauthorized", { status: 401 });
  }
  const processor = new TaskProcessor();
  await processor.processQueue();
  return NextResponse.json({ success: true });
}

export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
  return await handler(request);
}

export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
  return await handler(request);
}

/**
 * This is a factory class that creates Taskers.

export class TaskerFactory {
  createTasker(type?: TaskerTypes): Tasker {
    // TODO: Add more alternative Taskers in the future:

    // For now, we only have the InternalTasker.
    if (type === "internal") return new InternalTasker();
    // Default to InternalTasker
    return new InternalTasker();
  }
}

/** Shorthand for getting the default Tasker */
export function getTasker() {
  const taskerFactory = new TaskerFactory();
  return taskerFactory.createTasker();
}

1	# Manual test: 24h booking reminder emails with Mailhog
2	
3	## Context
4	The unit tests never run the full chain of booking → task row → cron → real email. They also never run `sendBookingReminderEmails`, which decides who gets emailed. This guide checks it all by hand against the local dev app, with Mailhog catching the emails. You can't wait 24 hours, so you move the task's `scheduledAt` into the past and call the cron endpoint yourself.
5	
6	Facts this relies on (checked in the code):
7	- Mailhog runs from `packages/emails/docker-compose`. It accepts mail over SMTP on **1025** and has a web UI on **http://localhost:8025** (`students.md` step 5).
8	- The app sends to Mailhog when `.env` has `EMAIL_SERVER_HOST='localhost'` and `EMAIL_SERVER_PORT=1025` (`.env.example:227-228`).
9	- The task queue runs only when someone calls **`GET /api/tasks/cron`** (`apps/web/app/api/tasks/cron/route.ts`). Locally nothing calls it automatically. It requires the header `Authorization: Bearer ${CRON_SECRET}` (`packages/features/tasker/api/cron.ts:8`). **`CRON_SECRET` isn't in `.env.example`**, so you have to add it.
10	- `BaseEmail.sendEmail()` skips sending in three cases: `INTEGRATION_TEST_MODE=true`, an active global "emails" kill-switch feature flag, or a fake SMS address (`_base-email.ts:32-59`).
11	- The handler only sends if the booking is still `ACCEPTED` **and** its `startTime` still matches the task payload. So only move the **task's** time, never the booking's.
12	
13	## 1. One-time setup
14	1. Start Mailhog: `cd packages/emails && docker compose up -d && cd ../..`, then open http://localhost:8025.
15	2. In the root `.env`:
16	   - `EMAIL_SERVER_HOST='localhost'` and `EMAIL_SERVER_PORT=1025`
17	   - add `CRON_SECRET=localtest` (any value works)
18	   - make sure `INTEGRATION_TEST_MODE` is not `"true"`
19	3. On Windows, copy it over again: `cp .env packages/prisma/.env` (`students.md` step 3).
20	4. Restart `yarn dev` so the new environment variables are loaded.
21	
22	## 2. Happy path: a reminder is scheduled and delivered
23	1. Log in as `pro@example.com` / `pro`. Pick an event type that **doesn't require confirmation** and is free.
24	2. In a private window, book it from the public page for a slot **at least 2 days out**, using an attendee email such as `guest@test.dev`.
25	   - The usual confirmation emails should show up in Mailhog. That proves SMTP works. Clear them with the Mailhog "Delete all" button or `curl -X DELETE http://localhost:8025/api/v1/messages`.
26	3. Check the task row, either in Prisma Studio (`yarn db-studio` → `Task`) or with SQL:
27	   ```sql
28	   SELECT id, "referenceUid", "scheduledAt", payload, attempts, "succeededAt", "lastError"
29	   FROM "Task" WHERE type = 'sendBookingReminderEmail' ORDER BY "createdAt" DESC;
30	   ```
```

47	## 3. Cancel and reschedule scenarios (acceptance criterion 3)
48	Clear Mailhog between scenarios. For each one, run the SQL from 2.3 and, where it applies, steps 2.4–2.5.
49	
50	| Scenario | How | Expected |
51	|---|---|---|
52	| Cancel | Book ≥2 days out, then cancel it from `/bookings` | The task row is **deleted**. Running the cron sends no reminder. |
53	| Reschedule to ≥24h out | Reschedule a booking to another day ≥2 days away | The old uid's task is deleted. A new task exists for the **new** uid with the new `scheduledAt`. After fast-forwarding and running the cron, the reminder shows the new time. |
54	| Reschedule to <24h out | Reschedule to a slot later today or tomorrow, under 24h away | The old task is deleted and no new task is created. This is the PR's stated design. |
55	| Booked <24h ahead | Book a slot under 24h away | No task is created. |
56	| Requires confirmation | Turn on "Requires confirmation" for an event type and book it | No task while the booking is pending. After approving it in `/bookings`, a task appears. |
57	| Stale-task guard | Book ≥2 days out, then in SQL change the **task's** payload `startTime` to a different ISO time, fast-forward, and run the cron | No email. The task is still marked `succeededAt`, because the guard returns without an error. |
58	| Host emails disabled | If the event type's advanced settings let you turn off host emails, turn them off and repeat the happy path | Only the attendee's email arrives. |
59	| Team event (team-member gap) | Only if team event types exist in this fork: book a collective event | Expected per the review: only the organizer and attendee are emailed, not the other hosts. |

61	## 4. Troubleshooting
62	- **401 from the cron:** `CRON_SECRET` doesn't match the header, or the dev server wasn't restarted.
63	- **Task `attempts` goes up and `lastError` is set:** the handler threw. Read `lastError`. It retries up to 3 times, with no minimum gap between retries.
64	- **Task succeeded but no email:** check the dev-server console for "Skipped Sending Email" (kill switch / `INTEGRATION_TEST_MODE`) and confirm Mailhog is listening on 1025.
65	- **No confirmation emails at all in step 2.2:** the SMTP environment variables aren't loaded. Recheck setup steps 2–4.
66	
67	## Notes
68	- All of this is done by hand in your own dev environment. No repo files change.
69	- If you want this automated later, the same flow fits a Playwright test using the repo's existing Mailhog E2E helpers (`E2E_TEST_MAILHOG_ENABLED=1`).
